why: Real devices, real numbers. A copy is judged on the phones and tablets people actually hold, not only on three desktop-ish widths. Every field here is a published device measurement, so both sides are captured with the same viewport, the same pixel ratio and the same safe insets.
how: The run takes one shot per device, per route, on both sides, named shot-<device>.png.
Each shot is taken with the browser's own device emulation at exactly width, height and dpr below, and with animations frozen (gate G10 needs that).
The device shot pages are kept in shots/<device>/ so a person can open the folder and see, side by side, exactly what that phone would show.
A device with no paired shot is unknown, and unknown blocks the lock.
rules: The device list is chosen once, before the first build, and never shrinks mid-run.
Both sides use the same list: a device on one side only is unknown, never a pass.
Phone-first targets start at the narrowest phone and fail earliest there; desktop-first targets still have to survive the phone.
Safe insets are honoured: content under the notch is a G14 failure, not a taste choice.
Each device shot is kept in shots/<device>/<route>.png, so the person can open the folder and compare phone to phone, not screenshot to screenshot.
